result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day written-notice convenience right and a refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, while Vendor has no convenience right during a term. However, allowing termination “in whole or in part” and stating that termination is without “other liability” go beyond the playbook and could permit service-level cherry-picking or be read to waive accrued or unrelated obligations. The placement of Section 9.4 after Section 9.5 is also suboptimal. The clause should be limited to termination without an early-termination penalty, while expressly preserving liabilities accrued before termination.
